title_en: Qingdao Zhongnan Property Management Co., Ltd., Nanjing Branch v. Xu Xiantai and Lu Suxia — dispute over property management contract
ruling_gist_en: 1. After an owner signs a property management service agreement with the property management company of the community, a property management service contract relationship is established between the owner and the property management company. As a party to the contract providing property management services, the property management company has the obligation to carry out property management in accordance with the contract, to require the owners to comply with the owners' covenant and the community property management regulations, and has the right to correct any acts that violate the owners' covenant and property management regulations, so as to maintain the normal property management order of the community and protect the common interests of all owners in the community. When an owner fails to rectify the acts violating the owners' covenant and property management regulations in accordance with the rectification requirements, the property management company, as a party to the contract, has the right to file a lawsuit in accordance with the law.

full_text_en:
Qingdao Zhongnan Property Management Co., Ltd., Nanjing Branch v. Xu Xiantai and Lu Suxia — dispute over property management contract

[Ruling Summary]

1. After an owner signs a property management service agreement with the property management company of the community where the owner resides, a property management service contractual relationship is established between the owner and the property management company. As a contracting party providing property management services, the property management company is obligated to carry out property management in accordance with the agreement, require owners to comply with the owners' convention and the community property management regulations, and has the right to correct acts that violate the owners' convention and property management regulations, so as to maintain the normal property management order of the community and protect the common interests of all owners of the community. When an owner fails to correct, as required by a rectification notice, acts that violate the owners' convention and property management regulations, the property management company, as a contracting party, has the right to file a lawsuit in accordance with the law.

2. With respect to the ownership of a courtyard green space adjacent to the house purchased by an owner, the mere fact that a salesperson of the real estate developer once orally promised the owner that "buying a first-floor house comes with a garden" and the fact that the courtyard green space is actually occupied and used by the owner shall not be sufficient grounds to determine that the owner has an exclusive right to use the courtyard green space. Since the courtyard green space is immovable property, the attribution of its right to use must be determined based on the formal commercial housing sales agreement formally signed by the buyer and seller of the house and the registration of property rights.

3. An owner shall not, in violation of the owners' convention and property management regulations, and based on personal interests, arbitrarily destroy or alter the courtyard green space adjacent to the owner's house. Even if the owner has an exclusive right to use the courtyard green space, if the courtyard green space is part of the community's green space, the owner, when using the courtyard green space, must also comply with the management provisions on community green space as stipulated in the owners' convention and property management regulations, and shall not arbitrarily destroy the courtyard green space, thereby harming the legitimate rights and interests of other owners of the community.

Plaintiff: Qingdao Zhongnan Property Management Co., Ltd., Nanjing Branch, domiciled at: West Kaicheng Road, South of Yuemin Road, Tangshan Street, Jiangning District, Nanjing City.
Legal Representative: Chen Xingwu, Manager of the Branch.
Defendant: Xu Xiantai, male, 52 years old, residing at: Qilin Jincheng, No. 188 Kaicheng Road, Yuemin Road, Tangshan Street, Jiangning District, Nanjing City.
Defendant: Lu Suxia, female, 39 years old, same address as Xu Xiantai.

The plaintiff, Qingdao Zhongnan Property Management Co., Ltd., Nanjing Branch (hereinafter referred to as Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch), filed a lawsuit with the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, due to a property management contract dispute with the defendants, Xu Xiantai and Lu Suxia.

Plaintiff's Allegations: On March 10, 2005, the defendants Xu Xiantai and Lu Suxia purchased a house in the Qilin Jincheng community managed by the plaintiff, and the house delivery procedures were completed on October 1 of the same year. In December of the same year, the two defendants renovated the house and arbitrarily destroyed the public green space outside the south balcony of the house, converting it into a cement floor and a fish pond. The above actions of the two defendants have seriously violated the relevant provisions of the *Zhongnan Qilin Jincheng Owners' Convention* and the *Zhongnan Qilin Jincheng Property Management Service Agreement*, infringing upon the legitimate rights and interests of other owners of the community. The plaintiff requested that the court order the two defendants to demolish the illegally constructed cement floor and fish pond and restore the original green space.

Defendants' Defense: 1. The plaintiff, Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch, has no right to file this lawsuit as the plaintiff in this case. 2. The real estate developer of the Qilin Jincheng community, Nanjing Changjin Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Changjin Company), promised the defendants when selling the house that buying a first-floor house comes with a garden. The courtyard outside the south balcony of the house purchased by the defendants was the garden promised by Changjin Company. Therefore, the defendants have the right to use the courtyard green space outside the south balcony, and others have no right to interfere with their act of altering the courtyard green space. 3. When the defendants altered the courtyard green space, the management personnel of Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch were aware of it but did not stop the defendants' alteration, indicating that Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch agreed to the defendants' alteration. Therefore, the defendants disagreed with restoring the courtyard green space to its original state and requested that the court dismiss Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch's claims.

Facts Found by the Court at First Instance:

On March 10, 2005, the defendants Xu Xiantai and Lu Suxia entered into a *Commercial Housing Sales Contract* with Changjin Company, agreeing that Xu and Lu would purchase one house in the Qilin Jincheng community developed by Changjin Company, with a total price of RMB 323,470. After the contract was signed, Xu and Lu paid the full purchase price in one lump sum.

The plaintiff, Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch, was entrusted by Changjin Company to provide preliminary property management for the Qilin Jincheng community. On October 1, 2005, the defendants Xu Xiantai and Lu Suxia completed the house delivery procedures. On the same day, Xu and Lu signed the *Zhongnan Qilin Jincheng Owners' Convention* and entered into the *Zhongnan Qilin Jincheng Property Management Service Agreement* with Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch. Article 2(5) of Chapter 3 of the *Zhongnan Qilin Jincheng Owners' Convention* stipulates that owners shall abide by the provisions of relevant government departments concerning house use and decoration and shall not arbitrarily change the use, appearance, or structure of the house and public facilities. Article 2(8) of that chapter stipulates that owners shall consciously maintain public order and environmental hygiene within the area and shall not engage in illegal construction, park vehicles indiscriminately, arbitrarily occupy or damage green spaces, pollute the environment, or create noise disturbing residents. Article 2(6) of Chapter 5 of the *Zhongnan Qilin Jincheng Owners' Convention* stipulates that the content of property management services includes the maintenance and management of courtyard green spaces and other facilities. Article 2(3) of Chapter 6 of the *Zhongnan Qilin Jincheng Owners' Convention* stipulates that owners shall not construct buildings or structures in courtyards, terraces, rooftops, green spaces, roads, or other areas or spaces for exclusive use. Article 2(4) of that chapter stipulates that owners shall not encroach upon or damage roads, green spaces, flowers, trees, artistic landscapes, and recreational, sports, or leisure facilities. Article 2(9) of the *Zhongnan Qilin Jincheng Property Management Service Agreement* stipulates that the property management services provided by Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch to owners include the maintenance and management of public green spaces, flowers, trees, and architectural features.

Outside the south balcony of the house purchased by the defendants Xu Xiantai and Lu Suxia in the Qilin Jincheng community, there is a courtyard green space. This courtyard green space is surrounded by wooden railings approximately 50 cm in height. Changjin Company reserved an access door on the south balcony when constructing the house. The sales contract between Xu, Lu, and Changjin Company did not specify the attribution of the right to use the courtyard green space. Xu and Lu have not yet obtained the House Ownership Certificate or the State-owned Land Use Right Certificate. In December 2005, when Xu and Lu were renovating the house in the Qilin Jincheng community, they altered the courtyard green space outside the south balcony of the house, destroying the original green space and laying a cement floor, building a flower bed, and constructing a fish pond in the courtyard. Consequently, the plaintiff, Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch, issued rectification notices to Xu and Lu on November 1, 2005, and March 21, 2006, respectively, requiring them to stop altering the courtyard green space and restore it to its original state. Xu signed for the rectification notices issued by Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch on two occasions. Because Xu and Lu did not rectify the situation as required by the property management requests, Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch filed a lawsuit with the court regarding this dispute in November 2006.

During the first instance, the defendants Xu Xiantai and Lu Suxia applied for witnesses to testify in court to prove that when they purchased the house at the Changjin Company sales office, the salesperson orally promised that buying a first-floor house comes with a garden. Xu also stated that he had only signed for a rectification notice from Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch once and had not checked the specific content of the notice at the time of signing.

The above facts are confirmed by the commercial housing sales contract signed by the defendants Xu Xiantai and Lu Suxia with Changjin Company, the *Zhongnan Qilin Jincheng Owners' Convention*, the *Zhongnan Qilin Jincheng Property Management Service Agreement*, on-site inspection photos, the rectification notices issued by the plaintiff Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch and signed for by Xu, witness testimony, and the statements of both parties. These facts are sufficient for determination.

The issues in dispute in this case are: (1) whether the plaintiff, Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch, is a proper litigant in this case and can file this lawsuit as a plaintiff; (2) whether the defendants, Xu Xiantai and Lu Suxia, have an exclusive right to use the courtyard green space outside the south balcony of the house they purchased in the Qilin Jincheng community; (3) whether the defendants, Xu Xiantai and Lu Suxia, have the right to alter the aforementioned courtyard green space.

Opinion of the Court at First Instance (Jiangning District People's Court, Nanjing):

1. The plaintiff, Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch, is a proper litigant in this case and has the right to file this lawsuit.

According to the facts of this case, the plaintiff, Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch, was entrusted by Changjin Company to provide preliminary property management for the Qilin Jincheng community. After the defendants, Xu Xiantai and Lu Suxia, purchased a house in the Qilin Jincheng community, they completed the house delivery procedures on October 1, 2005. On the same day, they signed the *Zhongnan Qilin Jincheng Owners' Convention* and entered into the *Zhongnan Qilin Jincheng Property Management Service Agreement* with Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch. Therefore, a property management service contractual relationship was established between Xu, Lu, and Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch. As a contracting party providing property management services, Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch is obligated to carry out property management in accordance with the agreement, require owners to comply with the owners' convention and the community property management regulations, and has the right to correct acts that violate the owners' convention and property management regulations, so as to maintain the normal property management order of the community and protect the common interests of all owners of the community. When an owner fails to correct, as required by a rectification notice, acts that violate the owners' convention and property management regulations, Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch, as a contracting party, has the right to file a lawsuit in accordance with the law.

2. Based on the facts of this case, it cannot be determined that the defendants, Xu Xiantai and Lu Suxia, have an exclusive right to use the courtyard green space outside the south balcony of the house they purchased in the Qilin Jincheng community.

The defendants, Xu Xiantai and Lu Suxia, claimed that a salesperson of Changjin Company had orally promised that buying a first-floor house comes with a garden, and witnesses confirmed that the salesperson had indeed made such an oral promise. According to the on-site inspection, the courtyard green space outside the south balcony of the house purchased by Xu and Lu in the Qilin Jincheng community is enclosed by railings, and Changjin Company reserved an access door on the south balcony when constructing the house. Based on this, the family of Xu and Lu could enter this courtyard green space, while other owners of the community could not. That is, from the design and construction of the courtyard green space, it appeared to be for the exclusive use of the family of Xu and Lu. However, based on the above facts, it cannot be determined that Xu and Lu have an exclusive right to use the courtyard green space outside the south balcony of the house they purchased in the Qilin Jincheng community. Since the courtyard green space is immovable property, the attribution of its right to use cannot be determined solely based on the actual occupation and use; it must be determined by the content of the agreement between the buyer and seller of the house and the registration of property rights.

First, even if a salesperson of Changjin Company had orally promised the defendants, Xu Xiantai and Lu Suxia, that buying a first-floor house comes with a garden, the *Commercial Housing Sales Contract* formally signed between Changjin Company and Xu and Lu does not explicitly stipulate the right to use the courtyard green space outside the south balcony of the house purchased by Xu and Lu. The oral promise made by the salesperson of Changjin Company occurred first, and the formal *Commercial Housing Sales Contract* was signed later. Since the *Commercial Housing Sales Contract* is a written contract, the agreement between the buyer and seller regarding the attribution of the right to use the courtyard green space should be determined by the content of the *Commercial Housing Sales Contract* formally signed by Changjin Company and Xu and Lu. According to this *Commercial Housing Sales Contract*, it cannot be determined that Xu and Lu obtained the right to use the courtyard green space outside the south balcony of the house at the same time they purchased the house.

Second, if the defendants, Xu Xiantai and Lu Suxia, had an exclusive right to use the courtyard green space outside the south balcony of the house they purchased in the Qilin Jincheng community, this fact should be explicitly recorded in the House Ownership Certificate and the State-owned Land Use Right Certificate. Given that Xu and Lu have not yet obtained the House Ownership Certificate or the State-owned Land Use Right Certificate, they cannot prove their exclusive right to use the courtyard green space with property right certificates. Therefore, the claim of Xu and Lu that they have an exclusive right to use the courtyard green space lacks factual basis.

In summary, based on the facts of this case, it can only be determined that the defendants, Xu Xiantai and Lu Suxia, have a general right to use the courtyard green space outside the south balcony of the house they purchased in the Qilin Jincheng community, and it cannot be determined that they have an exclusive right to use the courtyard green space.

3. The defendants, Xu Xiantai and Lu Suxia, are not entitled to arbitrarily alter the courtyard green space outside the south balcony of the house they purchased in the Qilin Jincheng community.

First, since it cannot be determined that the defendants, Xu Xiantai and Lu Suxia, have an exclusive right to use the courtyard green space outside the south balcony of the house they purchased in the Qilin Jincheng community, the defense argument of Xu and Lu that others have no right to interfere with their alteration of the courtyard green space cannot stand.

Second, according to the facts of this case, after the plaintiff, Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch, discovered that the defendants, Xu Xiantai and Lu Suxia, had altered the courtyard green space outside the south balcony of the house they purchased in the Qilin Jincheng community, it issued rectification notices to Xu and Lu on November 1, 2005, and March 21, 2006, respectively, requiring them to stop altering the courtyard green space and restore it to its original state. Xu signed for the rectification notices issued by Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch on two occasions. During the trial, Xu claimed that he had only signed for a rectification notice from Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch once and had not checked the specific content of the notice at the time of signing. However, he failed to provide evidence to prove this, and his claim that he signed without checking the specific content of the rectification notice is contrary to common sense. Therefore, this claim is not supported. Based on the facts that Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch served rectification notices to Xu and Lu on two occasions and filed a lawsuit with the court after Xu and Lu refused to rectify, it can be determined that Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch did not agree to the act of Xu and Lu in altering the courtyard green space. The defense argument of Xu and Lu that Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch was aware of their alteration of the courtyard green space but did not stop it, and therefore should be deemed to have agreed to the alteration, cannot stand.

Third, the *Zhongnan Qilin Jincheng Owners' Convention* signed by the defendants, Xu Xiantai and Lu Suxia, and the *Zhongnan Qilin Jincheng Property Management Service Agreement* entered into with the plaintiff, Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch, reflect their true intentions and do not violate the mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations. Therefore, they should be deemed lawful and valid. Consequently, the *Zhongnan Qilin Jincheng Owners' Convention* and the *Zhongnan Qilin Jincheng Property Management Service Agreement* are both binding on Xu and Lu, and the two defendants should perform their corresponding obligations in accordance with the *Zhongnan Qilin Jincheng Owners' Convention* and the *Zhongnan Qilin Jincheng Property Management Service Agreement*. According to the provisions of the *Zhongnan Qilin Jincheng Owners' Convention* and the *Zhongnan Qilin Jincheng Property Management Service Agreement*, Xu and Lu cannot destroy or arbitrarily alter the courtyard green space outside the south balcony of the house they purchased in the Qilin Jincheng community. Even assuming, for the sake of argument, that Xu and Lu have an exclusive right to use the courtyard green space, since this courtyard green space is part of the community's green space, and in accordance with the principle of public interest in property rights, when using the courtyard green space, Xu and Lu must also comply with the management provisions on community green space as stipulated in the *Zhongnan Qilin Jincheng Owners' Convention* and the *Zhongnan Qilin Jincheng Property Management Service Agreement*, and shall not arbitrarily destroy the courtyard green space, thereby harming the legitimate rights and interests of other owners of the community. Therefore, the act of Xu and Lu in arbitrarily altering the courtyard green space has violated the provisions of the *Zhongnan Qilin Jincheng Owners' Convention* and the *Zhongnan Qilin Jincheng Property Management Service Agreement*. The claim of Zhongnan Property Nanjing Branch requesting that Xu and Lu stop altering the courtyard green space, demolish the cement floor, fish pond, and flower bed, and restore the courtyard green space to its original state should be supported.

Accordingly, in accordance with Article 106, Paragraph 1, and Article 111 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China*, the Jiangning District People's Court of Nanjing rendered the following judgment on November 30, 2006:

The defendants, Xu Xiantai and Lu Suxia, shall, within 60 days from the date this judgment becomes legally effective, demolish the cement floor, fish pond, and flower bed they constructed in the courtyard green space outside the south balcony of the house they purchased in the Qilin Jincheng community, and restore the courtyard green space to its original state.

After the judgment was pronounced at first instance, neither party filed an appeal within the statutory period. The judgment of first instance has become legally effective.
